newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia central bank moves to stimulate exports.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia central bank moves to stimulate exports.

text.p: Indonesia's central bank, Bank Indonesia, said on Friday it had cut its bill of exchange discount rates by between one and 1.5 percent to stimulate exports.
The central bank said it had also issued a new regulation which enabled banks to sell drafts they had obtained from suppliers of specified exporters to Bank Indonesia.
The central bank said it had cut the bill of exchange discount rates for specified exporters to equal the Singapore interbank offered rate (SIBOR) from SIBOR plus one percent.
It said it also cut the bill of exchange discount rates for other exporters to SIBOR plus one percent from SIBOR plus 2.5 percent previously.
The bank did not detail the list of specified exporters.

The central bank said the discount rate for drafts obtained by banks from suppliers of specified exporters would be the three-month cut-off rate for short-term securities (SBPUs) plus or minus a certain margin.
It said the current margin was minus 0.5 percent.
Bank Indonesia said other elements of this facility included that the remaining period of the drafts should be at least 30 days and at 90 days at the longest.
It also said banks must have been "adequately healthy" in the past 12 months to get the facility.
The central bank said efforts should taken to encourage the trading of bill of exchanges resulting from exports and local trades in the secondary market.
Bankers said the list of "specified exporters" referred to by the central bank was drawn up by the Ministry of Industry and Trade.
